situation: During a football tournament, a boy from Brazil asks Kevin, a Cameroonian student: "Where exactly is Africa? Is it a country or a continent? Which seas surround it?"
Kevin knows that he is African, but he cannot describe the position of Africa on the world map.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Kevin cannot describe the position of Africa on the world map.
What questions did the Brazilian boy ask?
He asked where Africa is, whether it is a country or a continent, and which seas surround it.
How can Kevin learn to describe Africa?
He can study a map of Africa in his atlas, with its latitudes, oceans, seas and neighbouring continents.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to know the position, size and main physical features of our continent, Africa.

qa.q: Look at the map. Which oceans and seas surround Africa?
qa.a: Africa is surrounded by the Mediterranean Sea in the north, the Red Sea in the north-east, the Indian Ocean in the east and the Atlantic Ocean in the west.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Which important line of latitude crosses the middle of Africa? What does this tell us about its climate?
qa.a: The Equator crosses the middle of Africa. Most of Africa lies between the two tropics, so it is the hottest continent.

qa.q: What separates Africa from Europe and from Asia?
qa.a: The Strait of Gibraltar, about 14 km wide, separates Africa from Europe. The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, separates Africa from Asia.

qa.q: Africa covers about 30 million km² and has 54 countries. How does it rank among the continents?
qa.a: Africa is the second largest continent in the world, after Asia.

sum.title: I. Location and Size
sum.intro: The location and size of Africa can be described as follows:
items: Africa lies between latitudes 37°N and 35°S, and longitudes 17°W and 51°E. The Equator crosses its middle.
Africa is surrounded by the Mediterranean Sea, the Red Sea, the Indian Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean.
The Strait of Gibraltar separates Africa from Europe, and the Suez Canal separates it from Asia.
Africa covers about 30 million km². It is the second largest continent, with 54 countries.

qa.q: Most of Africa is made of high, flat land. What do we call this type of land, and why is Africa called a "plateau continent"?
qa.a: High, flat land is called a plateau. Africa is called a plateau continent because most of it is a plateau, with narrow coastal plains.

qa.q: What is the highest mountain of Africa, and what is the longest river?
qa.a: The highest mountain is Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) in Tanzania. The longest river is the Nile, about 6,650 km long.

qa.q: The African coastline has few bays and inlets. What problem does this cause?
qa.a: It has few natural harbours, so ports had to be built at great cost.

sum.title: II. Physical Characteristics
sum.intro: The main physical characteristics of Africa are the following:
items: Most of Africa is a high plateau, with narrow coastal plains.
The highest point is Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) in Tanzania. The lowest point is Lake Assal (−155 m) in Djibouti.
The Nile is the longest river in Africa (about 6,650 km). Lake Victoria is the largest lake.
The coastline is smooth, with few bays, so Africa has few natural harbours.

evaluation: Between which latitudes is Africa located?
Africa is located between latitudes 37°N and 35°S.
The Suez Canal separates Africa from Asia.
Why is Africa called a plateau continent?
It is called a plateau continent because most of its land is a high plateau.
remediation: Africa is the ______ largest continent in the world.
The highest mountain of Africa is ______.
The longest river of Africa is the ______.
The lowest point of Africa is Lake ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. second 2. 54 3. Strait of Gibraltar 4. Kilimanjaro 5. Nile 6. Assal
d.homework: Compare the climate of Douala, Garoua and Maroua. Which town is the wettest, and which is the driest? Ask an adult or use your textbook.
d.homeworkTag: This prepares Part 2: Climate, Soils and Relief of Africa.
